focus_band: P1 Performance & efficiency (deep dive) + full-band sweep; repo at v0.0.19

corpus.notes: Corpus is heavily perf-saturated: prior runs (2026-07-01 STATE, plus later runs that filed #151-#231 including an 2026-08-02 batch with enrichment comments and a 2026-08-04T02:22Z batch #221-#231) already cover nearly every hot path touched by v0.0.14-v0.0.19: scroll/repaint clones (#207), glyph/hinting caches (#205, #38), viewport-cull GlyphBox.h bug (#204), JS budget gaps (#213), sync image decode (#211), no transport reuse (#210), mirror restyle (#215), table-cap bypass (#220), grid blowups (#226/#227), Windows GUI-subsystem console loss (#208), plus the poll() layout_dirty over-invalidation (already documented in the 2026-08-02 comment on #22). This run therefore yielded few genuinely-new items; the two found are real and verified.

findings.title: Click hit-testing ignores paint order: links/controls in positioned (z>=0) overlay layers lose clicks to the in-flow content painted beneath them

No transport reuse (existing) — added: read_to_end_tolerant only checks response_is_complete on the timeout arm, so a connection-holding intermediary (CONNECT proxy, per the code's own comment) stalls EVERY request the full IO_TIMEOUT=20s even when the response is fully framed; tarpit hosts can pin the 4 workers 20s each for free. Also flagged the O(n^2) hazard of calling response_is_complete per read chunk instead of keeping incremental framing state.

Re-sighted: poll() sets layout_dirty=true unconditionally at entry (empty drains invalidate a valid layout cache) — already captured verbatim in the 2026-08-02 enrichment comment on #22; no new comment filed

duplicates_skipped: #22 comment (2026-08-02) already records poll()'s unconditional layout_dirty invalidation — re-sighted, skipped silently

Dependency spot-check (rustls 0.23.40, image 0.25.10, png 0.18.1, gif 0.14.2, rquickjs 0.9.0, webpki-roots 1.0.7): current, no known CVEs

overall_health: Good code, exceptionally well-audited backlog. The codebase moved fast (v0.0.14->v0.0.19 in ~5 weeks: layout cache, glyph cache, viewport cull, table-nesting cap, Windows polish) and prior review runs have already filed a dense, high-quality perf backlog (~40 open P1 items) covering essentially every hot path; the highest-leverage open work remains #210 (transport reuse — now with the proxied 20s-stall symptom attached), #170/#175 (layout asymptotics), #195/#213 (JS pipeline), and the cache-eviction cluster (#221/#194/#205/#176). This run's one new finding (#232 hit-test paint order) is a user-facing correctness gap in the otherwise-correct v0.0.17 z-order work. Tracker burn-down would now beat further audit passes.
